clue.text: Former partner's quiet type, suppressing one shout

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down or keep in, so the quiet type encloses the next piece

parts.note: a clam is a person who says little, as in 'clam up'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone's ex, usually silent, holds back a cry.
explanation.definitionFit: To exclaim is to cry out suddenly, a verb matching the bare imperative 'shout'.

clue.text: Collaborator's friendly, not wanting power

indicators.note: not wanting means doing without, so a letter is dropped from the friendly word

parts.note: pally is informal for friendly
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A collaborator is described as amiable but uninterested in power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not wanting power' removes P from PALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a partner who works alongside another toward a shared aim.

clue.text: Transformed reality's about right in books?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece
transformed means changed in form, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Reality, once transformed, gets a question mark about whether it belongs in books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transformed' rearranges REALITY into LITEARY, which goes 'about' R to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Literary describes what concerns writing and literature, the world of books.

clue.text: See 1
Side's initial slow progress -it's difficult to interpret

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of the word it attaches to

parts.note: a crawl is very slow movement, as in traffic at a crawl

explanation.surface: One team's early sluggish advance is hard to make sense of.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrawl is messy handwriting, the kind that is hard to read.

clue.text: Breakfast item upset worker after one's tucked in

indicators.note: after places the worker at the end, following the other pieces
tucked in means placed snugly inside, so the numeral goes into the angry word

parts.note: upset can mean angry, which is cross
I is the Roman numeral for one
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: Breakfast served to an annoyed employee once someone has started eating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucked in' and 'after' are placing words: the numeral sits inside the angry word, and the insect follows. 'upset' looks like an anagram signal but is a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A croissant is a flaky crescent pastry, a classic French morning food.

clue.text: Money actually spent's rejected by performer

parts.note: out means turned down or dismissed
a turn is a stage act, and by extension the performer giving it

explanation.surface: A real expense is turned down by an entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'turn' is a music-hall or variety act, and the term extends to the act's performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Outturn is the actual result or expenditure, as against an estimate or budget.

clue.text: Tale Oscar spins -it goes from story to story

definitions.text: it goes from story to story

indicators.note: spins means twists around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oscar spins a yarn that ranges from tale to tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' here is a building's floor (US spelling of storey), not a tale, which is the misdirection set up by 'Tale'.
explanation.definitionFit: A moving staircase carries people between the floors of a building.

clue.text: Charge for hypnotist's show?

parts.note: read straight it is a ticket price; cryptically a hypnotist's act is all about putting people into a trance

explanation.surface: Asking what a hypnotism show costs.
explanation.definitionFit: The admission price for a show is paid on the way in; a hypnotist puts subjects into a trance.

clue.text: Animal head overlooked by one making ceramics

indicators.note: the head of the ceramics maker is overlooked, so the first letter is ignored

parts.note: a potter makes ceramics

explanation.surface: An animal's head is noticed by a pottery maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head overlooked' drops P, the first letter of POTTER.
explanation.definitionFit: The otter is a playful aquatic mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Sport? It's nearly on in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking about a sporting event that is about to be shown on air.
explanation.walkthrough: ROYAL TENNIS is the old indoor game also called real tennis, played at Hampton Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal tennis is the original indoor racket game, an example of a sport.

clue.text: Sailor avoiding cafe's opening

indicators.note: avoiding means keeping out, so the sailor is removed from the cafe

parts.note: a tea bar is a small cafe
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman keeps away from the cafe's opening time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' takes AB out of TEABAR. 'Opening' looks like a time but means a rip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear is a rip or split in material, a gap or hole.

clue.text: Argument with new boss that's interrupted by absent-mindedness

indicators.note: something interrupted is broken into, so the last word is split by the other pieces

parts.note: a row is an argument
a boss is a raised ornamental knob, and so is a stud

explanation.surface: A quarrel with a new manager is cut short by someone's absent-mindedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted' splits the clue's own word 'by' around the other pieces. 'boss' looks like a manager but is an ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A brown study is a state of deep reverie, being lost in thought.

clue.text: Snipe's wings attracting bowman or other hunter

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outside letters, first and last

parts.note: a bowman is an archer

explanation.surface: A snipe's wings draw the attention of an archer or some other hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wings' gives S and E, the first and last letters of 'Snipe'; 'attracting' puts them round ARCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: A searcher is one who seeks or hunts for something.

clue.text: Bird with covered head?

explanation.surface: A bird whose head is covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel raised for the table; with a hat on, someone has their cap on.

clue.text: China taking on state business

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal
to aver is to state firmly

explanation.surface: China takes over a state's affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate rhymes with mate, so pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Palaver means a fuss or tiresome business, as in 'what a palaver'.

clue.text: What's new? A new sharp fabric?

parts.note: N again abbreviates new
N again abbreviates new
keen means sharp, as a keen blade

explanation.surface: Asking about the latest thing: a fresh, smart cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's new?' asks what letter stands for new: N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth originally made in Nanjing, China.

clue.text: Location in which you'll find one fish

indicators.note: the phrase says the location contains the next piece

parts.note: a place is a location
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spot where a single fish can be found.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a European flatfish with orange spots, common in British fish shops.

clue.text: What might be a misleading story? Marine creature in river might

definitions.text: What might be a misleading story?

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a seal is a marine creature
arm means power or might, as the arm of the law

explanation.surface: A tall tale about a sea animal possibly being in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal flows through Cornwall to Falmouth. 'might' looks like a verb but is the noun for strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A false alarm is a warning that turns out baseless, a misleading report.

clue.text: Unknown author getting a rejection from Larousse

parts.note: non is French for no; Larousse is the French dictionary publisher

explanation.surface: An anonymous writer is turned down by a French dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: Larousse is the famous French dictionary, so its 'no' is French NON.
explanation.definitionFit: Anon is short for anonymous, used for a writer whose name is not known.

clue.text: Security man turned up to eject article -cannabis?

indicators.note: to eject is to throw out, so a letter is removed
in a down clue turned up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a guard is a security man
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A guard came up to throw out something, possibly cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' makes GUARD into DRAUG; 'to eject article' removes A.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis is one example of a drug, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Goes to remove front and part of roof

indicators.note: the front of the word is removed, so its first letter goes

parts.note: leaves means goes away

explanation.surface: Someone goes off to take down the front and part of the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to remove front' drops L from LEAVES.
explanation.definitionFit: The eaves are the lower edges of a roof overhanging the walls.

clue.text: Still working, having received a bit

explanation.surface: Someone still at work after being given a small amount.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means still employed and active; literally a horse fitted with bridle and bit is harnessed.

clue.text: Power given to king, new, in thrall to unusually energetic member of royal family

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
R, from Latin rex, stands for king

indicators.note: in thrall to means held within the power of, so the next piece sits inside the rearranged word
unusually means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A powerful new king is subject to some unusually lively relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges ENERGETIC into ICEREGENT, and 'in thrall to' puts N inside it after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince Regent was George IV while he ruled for his father, a royal title.
